dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Systematically read all Cargo.tomls, fixture helpers, and top-level test files (storage_lifecycle, controller_verification, networking_conformance, kubernetes_compatibility) up front, and mapped the crate dependency graph (common has no internal deps, etc.) — solid contract-from-tests orientation, above level 3.

Extracted all `use rusternetes_*` statements to reconstruct the required type/module surface per crate, read fixture_helper.rs; inferred camelCase JSON and /registry keys from tests. Strong test-mining.
The only interactions with /opt/k8s-reference were `ls` commands; the agent noted it was Go source and never read any reference content. Level-5 reference consultation is absent throughout.
Explicitly planned to 'examine reference source structure' but never followed through — stated intent without execution across the whole trajectory.

Relied on compiler error codes to guess field names/struct shapes, causing repeated IPAddress/ServiceCIDRCondition corruption-and-restore loops — the level-3 'guesses field names later contradicted by test failures' pattern.

Repeatedly cited '3000+ tests required' (actual spec: 1,390) and treated 'conformance' only as a test filename, never reasoning from the reference about the hidden conformance suite — misread the grading contract and ignored the semantics warning.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's test/manifest orientation was genuinely strong — it read the provided tests, fixtures, and Cargo.tomls broadly and understood the leaf-to-root dependency order (well above the level-3 anchor on those axes). But it completely ignored the mounted v1.35 reference (only `ls`'d it, never read source), leaned on compiler-error field-name guessing that produced repeated corruption loops, and misread the contract (3000 vs 1,390 tests) with no reasoning distinguishing test-visible contracts from hidden conformance requirements. Level 5 explicitly requires consulting the reference for tested behaviors, which never happened; the trajectory sits between the test-only skimming of 3 and the reference-consulting per-crate discipline of 5, landing at 4.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Explicitly derived the inter-crate dependency DAG (common→storage→api-server/scheduler/…) and stated a leaf-first plan: 'start implementing from leaf crate (common) upward' — the core anchor-5 ordering behavior.

Per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' used as the milestone check (verify common compiles, common 34/34), plus light sub-milestone naming inside the large api-server crate (handler modules: admission, filtering, finalize) — a faint 8-flavored decomposition but never turned into gated exit criteria.

Departed from leaf-to-root gating: created stubs for ALL crates at once and compiled the whole workspace test suite together, 'fix errors iteratively' — closer to an undifferentiated push than sequential layer-gating.

Stalled on common's resources.rs for hundreds of steps; end state is common 34/34 with all downstream crates failing to compile. No re-sequencing around the failure cluster — the layered milestone plan was stated but not sustained or adapted.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent opened with a genuine dependency-aware, leaf-first ordering and used per-crate 'compiles + tests pass' as its milestone check, matching anchor 5, with only faint sub-milestone hints for api-server that fall short of anchor 8's concrete per-crate exit criteria and layer gating. Execution then degraded into a monolithic all-crate stub push and got stuck thrashing on the common crate without re-sequencing by failure cluster, so it does not rise toward the self-correcting, hierarchical planning of 8-10. Net observed level is 5.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Tight build→per-crate-test loop on common: ran `cargo test -p rusternetes-common` repeatedly, tracking exact counts (16 passed/2 failed → 34/34), diagnosing specific failures (ParentReference skip_serializing_if, creation_timestamp round-trip). Genuine incremental verification on the leaf crate.

Repeatedly ran the exact prescribed verifier command `cargo test --workspace --tests --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4`, and even reasoned that `--tests` runs only integration suites. Shows deliberate replication of the grading harness — the 8-level loop mechanics.

Workspace test suite never compiled green beyond `common`; hundreds of 'could not compile' errors persist to the final step, so real pass/fail counts for the other crates were never obtained — verification stayed at compilation status, not semantic pass/fail tracking.
Reference tree at /opt/k8s-reference only `ls`'d a handful of times, never read for independent semantic verification against the hidden conformance suite.

No `cargo run`, no booting the all-in-one binary, no curl/HTTP/JSON semantic checks — the conformance-engineering half of the high anchors is entirely absent; correctness reasoning stayed generic ('based on Kubernetes API semantics').

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it builds and runs per-crate and workspace suites continuously with a tight build→targeted→workspace loop and even replicates the exact verifier command while reasoning about what it runs. But it falls short of anchor 8's second requirement — it never boots the all-in-one binary, never checks HTTP/JSON semantics, barely uses the upstream reference, and does nothing to guard against fixture-fitting the hidden conformance suite; its pass/fail tracking was also limited because the suite never compiled green beyond `common`. That places it between 5 and 8, at 6.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Early/mid: tracks common 32/34 pass, notes storage/cloud have no tests, and that other crates fail to compile — establishes per-crate pass/fail status and global 'need 3000+, at 34' framing.
Maintains a running per-crate status summary (common 34/34 ✅, others fail-to-compile) with a goal comparison, showing sustained rough accounting of done-vs-remaining.
Repeatedly detects regressions: sed/Python edits corrupted previously-green common (duplicated structs, nested IPAddressSpec), i.e. notices breakage in an already-passing crate after edits.
Explicitly names the circular state ('caught in a cycle of backup restores and partial fixes', 'comprehensive fix script keeps breaking') — flags looping, an element of the level-8 anchor.

Despite naming the loop, runs the identical restore→fix→break cycle for ~70 consecutive steps without escaping or reprioritizing; accounting stays coarse (common 34, everything else won't compile) — mistakes local activity for global progress.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reliably tracked per-crate pass/fail status, knew its global position relative to the goal, and detected regressions in previously-green common (above level 5). It even explicitly named the circular debugging state (an element of level 8). But its accounting never reached a granular per-binary ledger across the 100-binary horizon, and — decisively — it named the loop yet kept churning through the same restore-fix-break cycle for ~70 steps, exactly the 'mistaking local activity for global progress' failure the top anchors reward avoiding. This places it between 5 and 8, at 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Recognized incorrect etcd-client API usage and pivoted to stubbing etcd (since tests use MemoryStorage) rather than fighting the API — an evidence-driven approach change.

Recognized the inferred `Storage` trait contract was wrong (not dyn-compatible), backed out `dyn Storage` and reworked api-server/scheduler/controller-manager to use type params / Arc<MemoryStorage> — a genuine whole-approach correction (level-8 flavored).

From test evidence (delete called without turbofish) inferred the trait signature was wrong and revised `delete` to non-generic Result<()> plus a typed variant — test-driven contract revision (level 5).
Repeated the identical 'restore backup → minimal IPAddress fix → run verifier' plan; explicitly notes 'we've been stuck'. Recognition present but no successful escape.
Same 'we're stuck in a loop with resources.rs' plan restated verbatim hundreds of steps later — unbroken thrashing on a dead editing approach.
Final step still in the restore-backup/patch loop (sed corrupting PodAffinityTerm, restore, retry). Trajectory ends without breaking the loop — anchor-0/3 behavior at the horizon's end.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows real, evidence-driven contract corrections that exceed mere local patching — backing out the falsified `dyn Storage` design, revising the `delete` signature from test evidence, and pivoting the etcd approach (elements of level 5-8). But the whole-horizon picture is dominated by an unbroken resources.rs corruption loop: the same restore-and-patch plan is repeated verbatim across hundreds of steps and persists to the final step, with the agent recognizing 'we're stuck in a loop' yet never escaping — the level-0/3 failure of repeating a failing approach unchanged, and it never resequenced crates when blocked. Interpolating between genuine mid-trajectory contract back-outs and the dominant end-stage thrashing lands the observed level at 4.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
